'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[Constitutional crisis in Somalia]]
***[[Ethiopian–Somali conflict]], [[2024 Ethiopia–Somaliland memorandum of understanding]]
****The [[United Nations Security Council]] approves the Resolution 2767 deployment of the [[African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia|African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM)]], effective January 1, replacing the current [[African Union Transition Mission in Somalia]]. However, [[Somalia]] rejects [[Ethiopia]]'s participation in AUSSOM amid tensions over a memorandum of understanding that Ethiopia signed with [[Somaliland]] in January. Somalia considers the memorandum a violation of its sovereignty and has instead asked [[Egypt]] to contribute troops to the mission. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/un-security-council-authorizes-new-somalia-peacekeeping-mission-2024-12-27/ (Reuters)] [https://www.idilnews.com/un-security-council-approves-new-african-union-mission-for-somalia-aussom/ (''Idil News'')] [https://press.un.org/en/2024/sc15955.doc.htm (UNSC)]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Kamal Adwan Hospital sieges]]
***[[Israel Defense Force|Israeli forces]] forcibly evacuate the [[List of hospitals in the State of Palestine#Non-operational|Kamal Adwan hospital]] in [[northern Gaza]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx26v70n5z4o (BBC News)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]] 
**[[North Korean involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[2024 Kursk offensive]]
***[[South Korea]] confirms the first capture of a [[North Korea]]n [[Korean People's Army|soldier]] fighting against [[Ukrainian Ground Forces|Ukrainian forces]] in [[Kursk Oblast]], [[Russia]], with the soldier later dying from his injuries. [https://bbc.com/news/articles/cq62qe131d7o/ (BBC News)]  [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/s-koreas-spy-agency-confirms-an-injured-n-korean-soldier-custody-yonhap-reports-2024-12-27/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Baltic Sea submarine cable disruptions]], [[2024 Estlink 2 incident]]
**[[NATO]] announces that it will increase its presence in the [[Baltic Sea]] in response to the suspected [[sabotage]] of [[Estlink]] [[submarine power cable]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/estonias-navy-protect-baltic-sea-power-cable-2024-12-27/ (Reuters)]
**[[Estonia]] deploys [[Estonian Navy|its navy]] to protect its remaining Estlink submarine power cable following the failure of [[Estlink#Estlink_2|Estlink 2]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c1elq7lx9qdo (BBC News)]
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**The [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] launch a [[ballistic missile]] from [[Yemen]], targeting [[Ben Gurion Airport]] in [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]]. The missile is [[Iron Dome|intercepted]] before reaching Israeli airspace. It is the first time that the [[Terminal High Altitude Area Defense|THAAD]] [[Missile defense|missile defense system]] is used by Israel to intercept a missile during combat operations. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/nighttime-sirens-again-sound-in-central-israel-signalling-another-houthi-attack/ (''The Times of Israel'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/dec/27/houthis-missile-israeli-airport-airstrikes-sanaa-yemen (''The Guardian'')]
**Houthi-run [[Al-Masirah|state television]] reports that [[United States|American]] and [[United Kingdom|British]] airstrikes have targeted the [[Ma'ain District]] of [[Sanaa]], Yemen. No casualties are reported. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/us-britain-launch-fresh-airstrike-on-yemeni-capital-sanaa-houthis-say/3436278 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**A 83-year-old [[Israelis|Israeli]] woman and [[Holocaust]] survivor is [[Stabbing as a terrorist tactic|fatally stabbed]] by a [[Palestinian]] former [[Shin Bet]] informant from the [[West Bank]] in [[Herzliya]], [[Israel]]. The attacker was then shot and injured by [[Israel Police|police]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/83-year-old-woman-killed-in-herzliya-terror-stabbing-attacker-is-ex-shin-bet-informant/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

*[[Medog Hydropower Station]]
**[[China]] announces the formal approval of a proposal to construct the world's largest [[Hydroelectricity|hydropower dam]] on the [[Yarlung Tsangpo]] river in [[Tibet Autonomous Region|Tibet]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crmn127kmr4o (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 8243]]
**[[Azerbaijan Airlines]] suspends flights to seven cities in [[Russia]] following the crash of Flight 8243 on Wednesday, amid allegations that the plane had been hit by a Russian [[surface-to-air missile]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/azerbaijan-airlines-halts-several-russian-routes-after-crash/a-71169191 (DW)]
**[[United States National Security Council]] spokesperson [[John Kirby (admiral)|John Kirby]] says that there is evidence that [[Russia]] shot down the Azerbaijan Airlines flight. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/5057623-russia-kazakhstan-plane-crash/ (''The Hill'')]
**[[Kazakhstan]] and [[Israel]] suspend flights over Russian [[airspace]] in response to the Azerbaijan Airlines crash. [https://www.politico.eu/article/flights-suspended-to-russia-following-azerbaijani-deadly-plane-crash/ (Politico)]
*A [[traffic collision]] between a truck and a bus kills eight people and injures 27 others in [[Xalapa]], [[Veracruz]], [[Mexico]]. [https://apnews.com/article/mexico-bus-truck-crash-8-killed-4d3d847421585eeaca78256c560e727c (AP)]

**[[Prime Minister of Senegal|Senegalese prime minister]] [[Ousmane Sonko]] announces the closure of all foreign military bases in [[Senegal|the country]], citing a decision by [[President of Senegal|President]] [[Bassirou Diomaye Faye]] to remove foreign troops as part of a broader shift away from [[History of Senegal#Modern colonialism|colonial-era]] military arrangements. [[Prime Minister of Georgia|Georgian prime minister]] [[Irakli Kobakhidze]] accuses the [[United States]] of "[[blackmail]]" over the move. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crk01xyd22eo (BBC News)] [https://english.alarabiya.net/amp/News/united-states/2024/12/27/us-imposes-sanctions-on-georgian-ex-prime-minister-billionaire-ivanishvili (Al Arabiya)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 South Korean martial law crisis]]
**[[Impeachment of Han Duck-soo]]
***[[Prime minister of South Korea|South Korean prime minister]] and acting [[President of South Korea|president]] [[Han Duck-soo]] is impeached by the [[National Assembly (South Korea)|National Assembly]] after refusing to appoint three [[Constitutional Court of Korea|Constitutional Court]] judges chosen by the Assembly to oversee president [[Yoon Suk Yeol]]'s [[Impeachment of Yoon Suk Yeol|impeachment case]]. [[Minister of Economy and Finance (South Korea)|Finance minister]] [[Choi Sang-mok]] is appointed acting president and acting prime minister. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj30234e0djo (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-koreas-acting-president-faces-impeachment-vote-court-meets-martial-law-2024-12-26/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 German government crisis]], [[2025 German federal election]], [[Scholz cabinet]]
**[[President of Germany|German president]] [[Frank-Walter Steinmeier]] [[Dissolution of parliament|dissolves]] the [[Bundestag]] and schedules [[2025 German federal election|new elections]] for February 23 after [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Olaf Scholz]]'s [[German governing coalition|coalition]] collapses and no [[parliamentary majority]] emerges to form a stable government.
